floor_history.headline: Floor 25 -> 4: ported the matched sibling CdControlF's solved shape (pin-free + base/elem two-step + do-while(0) loop-note wrap) and swept 480 init-order permutations; residual is a single a0-vs-saved

frontier.hypothesis: A loop.c-visible loop can be obtained without the LICM instruction cost, which would close the a0/saved inversion (the real-loop form already demonstrates that seating).
frontier.mechanism: loop.c emits NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG and re-weights refs, but also runs LICM on the loop; the two spellings tried both paid one-to-four extra instructions for the invariant -1 or for the shortened exit test.
frontier.next_probe: Keep the two-instruction '!= -1' exit test but make the -1 non-hoistable (compare against a value produced inside the loop); measure 'while (1) { ...; if (count == -1) break; }' and 'for (;;)' spellings purely as MEASUREMENTS to map the space (they are not sanctioned by the do-while(0) carve-out and must be judged on their own merits before any submission); and try a real loop enclosing only part of the body.

frontier.hypothesis: The a0-vs-saved priority inversion at the goto-form's score 4 can be flipped by changing a0's ref count or saved's live length rather than by loop visibility.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare divides by ALLOCNO_LIVE_LENGTH, so lengthening a0's live range or shortening saved's flips their relative priority; a0 has 2 refs (one inside the retry body) against saved's 3 (one inside), which under the wrap ties them closely enough that saved wins.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the spelling of the second CD_cw's first argument ('a0 & 0xFF' vs '(u8)a0' vs 'idx') — that is the most direct handle on a0's ref count — and move the 'saved = g_cd_callback_a;' read to immediately before the loop; sandbox each.

frontier.hypothesis: A side-by-side RTL comparison with the matched CdControlB explains why saved out-prioritises the a0 copy in CdControl but not in CdControlB.
frontier.mechanism: CdControlB matches with the same target seating and NO do-while(0) wrap; its structural differences are that it has no 'result' local (it uses 'status', assigned inside BOTH exit arms) and a trailing CD_sync block after the shared done: label.
frontier.next_probe: cc1 -da greg dumps of CdControl-at-4 and CdControlB, reading ';; Register dispositions:' and the conflict lists, to locate the exact allocno priority tiebreak; then test whether spelling CdControl's exit value the CdControlB way (set inside both arms rather than initialised before the loop) reproduces the ordering.
